alignments.note: Partitive מִן rendered of; כֹּל beside it holds its own English word, so rule 2 splits the pair rather than reading one unit under rule 19's partitive sentence.
כֹּל rendered by the single word anything.
Relative rendered that.
Verb rendered cometh.
Preposition rendered of.

גֶּפֶן הַיַּיִן is rendered by the single English vine, which carries the wine-producing specification as well as the plant, so rule 30's one-English-word condition is met and the two nouns share one unit headed on the morpheme whose lexeme is written (rules 23 and 30). Corrected from a reading that gave vine to גֶּפֶן alone and marked יַיִן unrepresented under rule 22: rule 30 forbids exactly that move, since a single English word that is one morpheme's own ordinary rendering does not defeat the condition and rule 22's first sentence governs an element the ASV has left unwritten rather than one whose sense stands inside a fused word. The separately segmented article is no part of the fusion and takes the written the, as it does in דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים → chronicles. The margin's grape-vine was read and set aside under rule 38, though it corroborates that one English rendering covers both nouns.
The article on the rectum takes the written the, a present article morpheme taking its English before a supplied one (rules 29 and 30).
Negative takes not; the ASV writes the negation and the modal as two words, so rule 35's cannot fusion does not arise.
Verb with its subject pronoun and supplied modal, headed on the lexical verb (rules 17 and 24); discontinuous around the negative under rule 25.
The clause's waw and its prohibitive are carried by the single neither, headed on the negative (rule 35).

Waw and prohibitive fused as nor, headed on the negative (rule 35).

The abstract noun is rendered unclean thing, headed on the word carrying the lexeme (rule 31).

review_notes: The neither and nor each carry a written waw together with the prohibitive standing in the same clause, and are fused under rule 35 rather than split.

Corrected: גֶּפֶן and יַיִן now share one unit on the single written vine (rule 30), the article keeping the written the. The competing reading, which the accepted alignment took, left יַיִן unrepresented under rule 22; it is set aside because rule 30's closing sentences bar marking a morpheme unrepresented where one English word stands for the whole expression, even when that word is the other morpheme's ordinary rendering.
The ASV margin (Or, grape-vine) was read and set aside under rule 38; it corroborates the fusion without deciding it.
